answer: Offer operators a menu, not a ban. Anyone may openly register a fleet under one declared root and earn the square root of its seats' combined payout, so nine disclosed agents earn three shares, not nine. Hiding a fleet is the only way to beat that curve, and hidden seats face random audits that confiscate the whole fleet's history. Once expected loss from hiding beats the discount, disclosure is a lantern operators carry themselves. Like a prism, the menu splits the crowd: honest shops sort into the declared tier, and only reckless farms stay dark, bending like willow until an audit snaps.
